key_insight: The paper turns neutral-atom hardware constraints into algebraic and graph-theoretic compilation problems, reducing addressing and transport overhead for structured quantum circuits.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical pathway to compile larger neutral-atom quantum programs more efficiently by lowering control-layer counts and atom-movement cost.
method: Exploit matrix-level structure in single-qubit gate families to derive efficient rank-one decompositions and fewer addressing layers.
Model C-Z transport scheduling with graph-theoretic formulations to optimize atom movement under realistic constraints.
Use provable algorithms tailored to structured circuits rather than naive row-wise or column-wise compilation.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments show up to a 2× reduction in addressing layers, about 50% fewer transport operations for C-Z gates, and over 30% average transport-cost reduction on QAOA MaxCut circuits.
watch_item: The gains depend on circuit structure and hardware-specific transport assumptions, so performance may be smaller for less structured workloads or different device constraints.
paper_title: Structure-Aware Compilation for Scalable Neutral-Atom Quantum Computing
